checks: The shared-base power is a bounded convex body with interior and product fibers. The weighted measure is supported on the required mixed lattice, and strict separation from the power forces a positive-depth center into it.

Independent exact cap evaluation reproduces the four midpoint masses (1,5,5,3/2). For the base-two cap the shifted mass is 5−δ+(-δ)_+, strictly below 21/4 when |δ|<1/8. The other three caps have unchanged off-base statuses on this neighborhood.

The centered uniform conditional law has support in [-5,5]. The exponential chord bound and cosh inequality yield exp(−kε²/50) in both tails. The untilted pure-base exclusion and averaging cap give uniform base-two and mean-five conclusions.

After a subsequence with extended-real tilt limit, finite strict discrete concavity gives only one or two adjacent maximizers; at either infinite limit the endpoint exponent dominates. All off-set weights are exponentially small. For a mark separated from their midpoint segment, the nearest-point normal gives a one-sided conditional deviation of at least its distance, or captures none if the continuous coefficient vanishes.

The contradiction with polynomial β_k is uniform over any infinitely chosen bad centers. Since projection keeps the integer base and the limiting segment has adjacent integer endpoints, every projected accumulation point is a midpoint mark. Averaging permutations preserves depth because each containing cap contains at least one orbit point.
Source 7d9bc9c2dd92ae95 §§2–4 explicitly states the open bad neighborhoods and the tilted quantifier. Its auxiliary correction and fiberwise join are outside this review.

dependencies.hypotheses: Take n=1 and continuous dimension k, and apply the finite Borel measure formulation to the tilted probability. It is supported on Z×R^k and has total mass one, giving 1/[2(k+1)] for closed halfspaces.

overlap.comparison: Gives existence of depth β_k for each powered measure, but no projection guarantee. The present theorem provides the opposing original-depth conclusion uniformly over all such centers.

readability: Read 'within 1/8' as the open neighborhood |δ|<1/8, as in the source and as used by the convergence proof. The left endpoint δ=−1/8 at base two gives equality 21/4, so a closed neighborhood would be too broad.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: For every integer-only tilt sequence, all sufficiently late Helly-depth centers in the shared-base powers project by averaging to points of original normalized depth below one quarter.
